correctness.rationale: Exact conditional beta and transverse-spherical fourth moments derive the full orthogonal gradient Gram decomposition, including normalization 4tr(AA*)/(d+2). A 2x2 planar-radial diagonalization and strict comparison a>1/2 yield all eigenvalues, multiplicities and extremal symmetry transitions. The equation d(d-2)=8cos²L admits interior solutions only for d=3. The analytically derived small-L expansion proves both sharp constants. An independently assembled full Gram checker passed 200 assertions in 5 dimensions and 10 aperture values; finite tests were not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: A full-text statement-level comparison distinguishes the new Dirichlet gradient concentration operator from the previously published scalar-value quadratic-lune spectra (2026) and general tensor/vector Slepian formulations (2004, 2020, 2021). The scalar results have two transitions arccos(±2/d) in every dimension, while the new derivative spectrum has transitions only at dimension three and at different apertures. The earlier vector theory gives machinery for constructing a concentration matrix, but not this explicit all-dimensional wedge spectrum or branch ordering. Searches do not establish global historical uniqueness; this is best-knowledge originality with identified residual risk.
residual_risks: No search is an exhaustive historical-priority certification; implicit equivalent derivations may exist in older or unindexed vector-spherical-harmonic literature.
The general vector Slepian setup is broad enough to assemble the relevant finite matrix, so only the explicit evaluated spectrum, ordering and exceptional transition classification are claimed.

The 2017 and 2020 primary papers include powerful exact scalar Slepian machinery; the priority claim excludes that machinery, and an unevaluated downstream specialization cannot be ruled out without independent historical examination.
